messages.subject: Applying MSstats to TMT data
parts:
Hi Olga and Meena!

I'm trying to apply MSstats for protein quantification based on TMT (isobaric labeling) data. I'm using version 2.4.0 from Bioconductor with R 3.1.2.
In a TMT experiment, multiple samples are multiplexed into one LC-MS/MS run; quantification happens via reporter ions that are detected in MS2 spectra (same as iTRAQ). I have a workflow that can give me intensities for the different reporter ions ("channels" - 6 in my case) together with the identification of the corresponding peptide. If a peptide is identified in multiple MS2 spectra, I get multiple quantitative observations for it.
What I want to do is aggregate the reporter ion intensities to protein abundances, based on the associated peptide identifications.

MSstats doesn't directly support TMT as a quantification method, but it supports stable isotope-labeled references, so I figured I could "decouple" my six TMT channels into multiple "conditions" with light and heavy isotope intensities.
In more detail: My TMT channels are called 126, 127, 128, 129, 130 and 131 (after the masses of the reporter ions). 126 and 131 are two references, and I want to quantify 127/126, 128/126, 130/131 and 129/131. In my input data for MSstats ("raw data"), I have created four "conditions" for these four comparisons. In each, the reference channel is encoded as the intensity of the heavy isotope, and the other channel as the intensity of the light isotope. If a peptide was identified multiple times (see above), I encoded the different observations as multiple "fragment ions" of the same peptide. (I'm currently only dealing with a single TMT run, so there are no biological/technical replicates.)

My first question is: Do you agree that this encoding doesn't violate any of the basic assumptions/constraints for MSstats?

Now, when I try to run the MSstats analysis on this data, I unfortunately encounter errors (due to missing values). This happens after "dataProcess" - i.e. running "dataProcess" works, but the result causes errors in "dataProcessPlots(type="ConditionPlot")" and "quantification". I have attached a subset of my input data (two proteins) in the file "part.RData", so you can replicate the following steps:

> load(file.path(base.dir, "part.RData"))
> part.proc <- dataProcess(part)

For "dataProcessPlots", you might consider wrapping the code for plotting each protein in a "tryCatch" call. This would prevent the function from crashing if there's a problem with one protein; you could just print an error in this case and continue plotting the other proteins. (If errors could be avoided, that would be even better, of course.)

The "quantification" function crashes if a protein cannot be quantified due to missing values. In some such cases there may simply be no way to quantify the protein, but this should be handled more gracefully. Again, "tryCatch" could help here, but filtering out the unquantifiable cases beforehand may be even better. For me as a user it is difficult to know which missing data can be tolerated and which which would lead to failures, which is why I believe MSstats should handle this.

I hope you can address these issues.


Cheers

Hendrik
